# closurectl 1.0.0

The first stable closurectl release provides attended incident containment for
exact GitHub Actions workflows and runs, npm token IDs, and AWS IAM role
sessions, with provider-independent planning and signed closure receipts.

Highlights:

- strict GitHub, npm, and AWS inventory-to-draft provenance followed by
  human-confirmed draft-to-graph construction;
- TTY incident wizard with final plan review and explicit graph creation;
- read-only clean-machine checks for independent provider recovery identities;
- fail-closed output/input alias checks that protect provider configs, keys,
  and incident artifacts from destructive path collisions;
- immutable execution previews, hash-chained journals, read-only resume, and
  independent observer evidence;
- unique preview-bound AWS role-session deny policies protected by IAM
  `RoleId`;
- deterministic offline HTML reports bound to separate evidence and signed
  receipts;
- Python wheel and sdist plus Linux x86-64/arm64, Windows x86-64, and macOS
  x86-64/arm64 executables.

Compatibility and support commitments are documented in
`docs/COMPATIBILITY.md` and `SUPPORT.md`. Provider permissions and tested CLI
versions are documented in `docs/PROVIDER_REQUIREMENTS.md`.

## Verify downloads

Download the release files and verify every checksum:

```bash
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS.txt
```

Verify GitHub artifact attestations against this repository:

```bash
gh attestation verify closurectl-linux-x86_64 --repo patcGM/closurectl \
  --signer-workflow patcGM/closurectl/.github/workflows/release.yml
gh attestation verify closurectl-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl --repo patcGM/closurectl \
  --signer-workflow patcGM/closurectl/.github/workflows/release.yml
```

Repeat `gh attestation verify` for the exact artifact used on your platform.
The signed tag, successful full CI run, independent review, and all destructive
provider drills are checked on the exact release commit before publication.
